questions.question: What inference rule combines CNF clauses to derive conclusions?
questions.explanation: Resolution is a complete inference rule for propositional logic in CNF.

questions.question: What theorem states that Γ, A ⊢ B implies Γ ⊢ A→B?
questions.explanation: The deduction theorem relates entailment and implication in formal logic.

questions.question: What type of validity requires truth preservation in all models?
questions.explanation: Semantic consequence is model-theoretic validity, requiring truth in all interpretations.

questions.question: What type of validity is based on derivability using inference rules?
questions.explanation: Syntactic consequence is proof-theoretic validity based on formal derivation.

questions.question: What property states that every semantically valid formula is provable?
questions.explanation: Completeness ensures semantic consequence implies syntactic consequence.

questions.question: What property ensures no contradictions can be derived in a system?
questions.explanation: A consistent system cannot prove both A and ¬A for any formula A.

questions.question: What proof system uses introduction and elimination rules?
questions.explanation: Natural deduction is a structural proof method with rules for introducing and eliminating connectives.

questions.question: What Gentzen-style proof system uses sequents?
questions.explanation: Sequent calculus represents logical arguments as sequents (Γ ⊢ Δ).

questions.question: What theorem states that removing the cut rule preserves provability?
questions.explanation: Cut elimination is a fundamental theorem showing proofs can avoid the cut rule.

questions.question: What correspondence links proofs to programs and propositions to types?
questions.explanation: The Curry-Howard correspondence establishes a deep connection between logic and computation.

questions.question: What sequent-calculus rule lets a proof use an already-derived lemma as a premise?
questions.explanation: Cut composes two derivations into one.

questions.question: What property of a proof system means every provable formula is semantically valid?
questions.explanation: Soundness: Γ ⊢ φ implies Γ ⊨ φ.

questions.question: What symbol denotes semantic consequence (truth in all models)?
questions.explanation: ⊨ marks model-theoretic consequence, unlike syntactic ⊢.

questions.question: What principle derives any statement from a contradiction (⊥ ⊢ φ)?
questions.explanation: From a falsehood, anything follows.

questions.question: What is a model that makes all premises true and the conclusion false called?
questions.explanation: A countermodel witnesses semantic invalidity.

questions.question: Premises: (1) If the server is patched, the exploit fails. (2) If the exploit fails, the data stays safe. (3) The data did not stay safe. Chaining (1) and (2) and applying modus tollens with (3), what follows about the server?
questions.explanation: p→q and q→r yield p→r by hypothetical syllogism; with ¬r, modus tollens gives ¬p.

questions.question: A resolution refutation uses the clauses (¬p∨q), (p), and (¬q∨r). Resolving the first two clauses produces q; resolving that result with the third clause yields which single literal?
questions.explanation: (¬p∨q) resolves with (p) on p to give (q); (q) resolves with (¬q∨r) on q to give (r).

questions.question: In a 16-row truth table over p, q, r, s, how many rows are counterexamples to the argument p→q, r→s, p∨r ⊢ q∨s?
questions.explanation: This is constructive dilemma, a valid form: whichever of p or r holds forces q or s, so no row makes all premises true with a false conclusion.

questions.question: A proof system derives p∧¬p from an empty premise set. Which metatheoretic property — that every provable formula is semantically valid — must fail?
questions.explanation: p∧¬p is unsatisfiable, so ⊢ p∧¬p holds while ⊭ p∧¬p — violating soundness (and consistency).

questions.question: Premises p→q and ¬p; conclusion ¬q. Under the assignment p=False, q=True both premises are true while the conclusion is false. What does this assignment demonstrate about the argument?
questions.explanation: p→q = F→T = T and ¬p = T, yet ¬q = F: a true-premises/false-conclusion row — the denying-the-antecedent form is invalid.
